name: Sort and Compare
summary: Two strings are anagrams exactly when their sorted characters match. Sort both, then compare character by character, stopping at the first difference.
visualizationIntent: init: if the lengths differ, answer is immediately false. Otherwise sort both strings and show them as two aligned character rows. loop: the i cursor compares the two rows position by position; matching positions turn green. check: the first mismatch flips answer to false and stops. return: whether the two sorted rows matched everywhere.

lineExplanations.4: Report false immediately on a length mismatch.
lineExplanations.8: Assume they match until a difference is found.
lineExplanations.10: Compare the two characters at this position.
lineExplanations.11: A mismatch means they are not anagrams.
lineExplanations.13: Otherwise advance to the next position.

syntaxExplanations.1: class Solution: defines the class wrapper expected by the platform.
syntaxExplanations.2: def isAnagram(self, s, t): receives the two strings.
syntaxExplanations.3: if len(s) != len(t): is true when the lengths differ.
syntaxExplanations.4: return False rejects strings of different lengths.
syntaxExplanations.5: s_chars = sorted(s) makes a sorted list of s's characters.
syntaxExplanations.6: t_chars = sorted(t) makes a sorted list of t's characters.
syntaxExplanations.7: i = 0 starts the comparison at the first position.
syntaxExplanations.8: answer = True assumes a match until proven otherwise.
syntaxExplanations.9: while i < len(s_chars): compares every position.
syntaxExplanations.10: if s_chars[i] != t_chars[i]: is true at the first difference.
syntaxExplanations.11: answer = False marks the strings as not anagrams.
syntaxExplanations.12: break stops at the first mismatch.
syntaxExplanations.13: i = i + 1 advances to the next position.
